chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Shave the young child who is 'al-qaza', and 'al-qaza' is that he shaves one part and leaves one part."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Qaza in Islamic shaving rituals for children?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Al-Sakuni to Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the etiquette of shaving a child's head by prohibiting 'al-qaza' (partial shaving), a practice often associated with pre-Islamic ignorance or superstition. It emphasizes completeness and uniformity in grooming, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on purifying customs from arbitrary traditions while maintaining the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt.
